body.heading: Morning-you has very little willpower
paragraphs: The person who wakes up in your bed tomorrow is tired, short of time and not at their most decisive. Evening-you, by contrast, has a whole day of perspective and a few spare minutes. It is only fair that evening-you does some of the work.
This is environment design across time: your calmer self prepares the ground so your sleepier self can simply follow it.

body.heading: The classic three
paragraphs: Lay out what you will wear, so the morning holds one decision fewer. Put the bag, keys and anything leaving the house with you by the door, in one place, every night.
Prepare the first step of your morning intention: oats in the bowl, book on the pillow, shoes by the door, water by the bed. The morning then begins with doing, not with hunting and deciding.

body.heading: Keep it under ten minutes
paragraphs: A setup routine that takes half an hour will be abandoned by Friday. Aim for a few small acts that fit inside the ordinary end of your evening — while the kettle boils, say, or right after you brush your teeth.
Some nights it will not happen, and the morning will be scrappier. That is fine. The routine is a gift you give most days, not another obligation to feel guilty about.

takeaway: Let evening-you do a few kind minutes of work that morning-you will be grateful for.
